title: Scalar tensor coefficient respects the two unit maps
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $F$ any $\mathcal O_X$-module. Write $S_f$ for scalar restriction, $U=\mathcal O_X$, $v:\mathbf1\to S_fU$ for scalarUnitMorphism, and $c_{F,G}:S_fF\otimes_k S_fG\to S_f(F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}G)$ for scalarTensorCoefficient [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations]. Both morphism equalities hold: $(S_fF\mathbin{\triangleleft}v);c_{F,U};S_f(\rho_F)=\rho_{S_fF}$ and $(v\mathbin{\triangleright}S_fF);c_{U,F};S_f(\lambda_F)=\lambda_{S_fF}$. No cohomology classes occur in these equalities.

source.place: Cohomology, section-cup-product, Lemma 20.31.1 (Tag 0FKU); Tag 01F7; Modules, Tags 0096 and 01CA

proof.text: Use the sheafification adjunction and monoidal tensorator of the sheaf inclusion to check the two maps on elementary tensors. The constant-sheaf adjunction defining the scalar-unit map makes its presheaf component send r to scalarMap(f,U)(r) on every open U. The coefficient map sends a pure tensor to tmulSection of its factors, by exists_scalarTensorCoefficient.

On s tensor r, the right module unitor after scalarTensorCoefficient returns scalarMap(f,U)(r) times s, which is r times s in the scalar module. On r tensor s, the left module unitor returns the same scalar multiple. The corresponding scalar unitors have these actions as well. Pure tensors generate the sectionwise tensor product. The sheafification adjunction and the unit coherence of the inclusion identify these sectionwise equalities with the claimed sheaf morphism equalities. The argument applies also to the zero module and empty scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem scalarTensorCoefficient_unit
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (F : X.Modules) :
    ((scalarSheaf f F) ◁ scalarUnitMorphism f) ≫
        scalarTensorCoefficient f F (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) ≫
        scalarHom f (ρ_ F).hom = (ρ_ (scalarSheaf f F)).hom ∧
    (scalarUnitMorphism f ▷ (scalarSheaf f F)) ≫
        scalarTensorCoefficient f (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) F ≫
        scalarHom f (λ_ F).hom = (λ_ (scalarSheaf f F)).hom
